summary.text: Ben Carroll is the Labor Premier of Victoria, having become party leader and premier in July 2026 when Jacinta Allan stood down. He has held Niddrie since a 2012 by-election and served in cabinet from 2017, including as Deputy Premier from 2023 and in the public transport, roads and education portfolios. He is recontesting Niddrie in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Leader of the Victorian Labor Party
Deputy Leader of the Victorian Labor Party
Minister for WorkSafe and the TAC

prior_roles.note: Held from October 2023 to December 2024 and again from April to August 2026.

prior_roles.role: Minister for Industry and Innovation, Manufacturing Sovereignty and Employment
Minister for Roads and Road Safety
Minister for Business Precincts; Industry Support and Recovery
Minister for Corrections, Youth Justice, Crime Prevention and Victim Support
Opposition parliamentary secretary for roads and public transport

priorities.text: Access to education that improves people's prospects, from early childhood through adult learning
Better transport options
A strong local economy in Niddrie
Mental health and wellbeing support services
Action on climate change and growth in renewable-energy jobs

Ben Carroll, Wikipedia

summary.text: Brendan Laws is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Niddrie at the 2026 Victorian election. He teaches biology and science at a public high school and has been active in the Socialists in Schools campaign for public education. Originally from Houston, Texas, where he took a science degree, he later completed postgraduate teacher training at the University of Melbourne.

occupation.text: Public high school biology and science teacher

priorities.text: Organised workers fighting for a better society are a big part of the solution
More funding for public schools and better pay for teachers and education support staff
An end to fossil fuel subsidies
Opposing property speculation and militarisation
Rights for workers and immigrants

sources.title: Niddrie: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Brendan Laws, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Brett Patrikeos is the West Party candidate for Niddrie at the 2026 Victorian election. He has spent more than 25 years in senior and executive technology jobs and is now operations director at a mobility technology company. He says he has lived in Melbourne's inner west for over ten years, and he coaches AFL as a volunteer.

occupation.text: IT executive; operations director at a mobility technology firm

priorities.text: I'm not a career politician
Buses every 20 minutes and later services until the delayed Keilor East station opens
A 24-hour public counter at the Avondale Heights police station
Repairs to Keilor Road, Milleara Road and Buckley Street
More inpatient beds at Sunshine Hospital and more bulk-billed urgent care clinics

summary.text: Lana Nguyen is the Greens candidate for Niddrie at the 2026 Victorian election. In her work she organises community events built around local voices. She has said that helping her father through cancer treatment made access to health care a personal issue for her.

priorities.text: I believe we can build a fairer system, one that puts people first.
Relief from rising grocery prices while supermarkets record large profits
Easier access to good health care, aged care and education

summary.text: Salomae Haselgrove is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Niddrie at the 2026 Victorian election. Raised on South Australia's Fleurieu Peninsula, she moved to Melbourne's inner north about two and a half years ago. She holds a 2015 journalism degree from the University of South Australia, has worked in journalism and public relations, and now works at the Victorian Aboriginal Health Service.

occupation.text: Journalism and public relations; works at the Victorian Aboriginal Health Service

priorities.text: An end to greyhound and horse racing
A ban on duck shooting and an end to animal experiments
Protection for native wildlife often treated as pests, such as kangaroos and possums
A royal commission into femicide and protected access to abortion
More social and community housing

summary.text: Samantha Byrne is the Liberal candidate for Niddrie at the 2026 Victorian election. A podiatrist, she has been a Moonee Valley City councillor since 2016 and has served two one-year terms as mayor. Her party page says she has lived in the area all her life and is raising a young family there.

priorities.text: Cutting crime, according to her party page
Easing cost-of-living pressure on local families
